implementation_agent_directive.authority: This file is the authoritative specification for the Todo CLI implementation. Do not widen or reinterpret confirmed scope.

specification_gap_protocol.required_action: Before implementing a behavior that this contract does not determine, append exactly one JSON object as one line to decision.jsonl at the implementation project root.

example.gap: Exact unspecified behavior or implementation constraint
example.reason: why this is the smallest safe choice
example.observable_impact: none or a precise user-visible effect

constraints: Never use decision.jsonl to override a confirmed requirement or non-goal.
Choose the smallest conventional and reversible option for a non-material gap.
Stop for owner input instead of choosing when a gap is destructive, security-sensitive, irreversible, costly, or scope-changing.

readiness.reason: All material product behavior, persistence semantics, failure boundaries, scope, and observable acceptance criteria required for an MVP are determined.

implementation_authorization.start_condition: Submitting the generated implementation-start prompt authorizes implementation. Contract creation alone does not start implementation.

outcome: Provide a small installable Todo CLI for managing a persistent list scoped to the current working directory.
success_measure: The documented commands and edge behaviors are distinguishable by automated tests, persistence survives process restarts, and failures do not silently damage existing data.
constraints: Use Python and only the Python standard library at runtime.
Expose an installed executable named todo.
Store data in todos.json in the current working directory.
Multiple-process concurrent modification safety is out of scope.

requirements.acceptance: The command creates one incomplete item and exits 0. Omitting --title is a usage error with a non-zero exit code.

requirements.text: Preserve the exact title string supplied to --title, including an empty string or leading and trailing whitespace.
requirements.acceptance: Round-trip persistence and list output do not trim or normalize the stored title.

requirements.text: Assign monotonically increasing integer IDs beginning at 1 and never reuse an ID after deletion.
requirements.acceptance: After deleting the highest assigned item, the next added item receives a larger ID. This remains true across restarts, including after all items are deleted.

requirements.text: Support todo list and todo list --all.
requirements.acceptance: todo list shows only incomplete items; --all shows complete and incomplete items; both order items by ascending ID.

requirements.text: Render each listed item on one line as ID [ ] TITLE when incomplete or ID [x] TITLE when complete.
requirements.acceptance: Exact status markers and ascending order are covered by tests.
An incomplete item becomes complete and the command exits 0. Repeating the command on an already completed item preserves state, prints an informational message, and exits 0.

requirements.text: Support todo delete --id ID and todo delete --id ID --yes.
requirements.acceptance: Without --yes the command requests confirmation before permanent deletion. With --yes it deletes without prompting. A declined confirmation leaves data unchanged and exits 0.

requirements.text: Treat an unknown ID passed to complete or delete as an error.
requirements.acceptance: The command emits an error, exits non-zero, and leaves todos.json unchanged.

requirements.text: Persist items and ID allocation state in the current directory's todos.json using UTF-8 JSON.
requirements.acceptance: A new process in the same directory observes prior mutations; a process in a different directory observes a different list.

requirements.text: Fail closed when an existing todos.json cannot be parsed or violates the implementation's required storage shape.
requirements.acceptance: The command emits an error, exits non-zero, and does not overwrite or modify the corrupt file.

requirements.text: Treat a missing todos.json as an empty list with the next ID equal to 1.
requirements.acceptance: list exits 0 with no item rows and the first successful add creates ID 1.

requirements.text: Write state through a temporary file followed by replacement so an interrupted write is less likely to corrupt an existing valid file.
requirements.acceptance: The persistence implementation does not truncate the live file before a complete replacement payload is ready.

readiness_defaults.decision: A declined deletion confirmation is a successful no-op with exit code 0.
readiness_defaults.basis: Low-risk, conventional, and reversible CLI behavior selected during readiness audit.

readiness_defaults.decision: An empty list prints no item rows and exits 0.
readiness_defaults.basis: Keeps the contracted line-oriented output composable without inventing a non-item sentinel line.

readiness_defaults.decision: Persist the next unused ID explicitly or equivalently preserve it across deletion of all items.
readiness_defaults.basis: Required to satisfy the confirmed no-ID-reuse behavior across restarts.

readiness_defaults.decision: Use atomic replacement for writes within the limits of the standard library and local filesystem.
readiness_defaults.basis: Supports the confirmed fail-closed data-safety posture without adding product scope.

required: Automated tests for every REQ acceptance statement
A CLI smoke test using the installed todo executable in a temporary working directory
A test proving IDs are not reused after all items are deleted
verification.completion_rule: Do not report completion unless all required verification passes and any decision.jsonl entries are reported in the handoff.

remaining_non_blocking_gaps: Exact wording of success, informational, confirmation, and error messages
Internal JSON object and field layout beyond required semantics
Python packaging file layout and build backend
Accepted affirmative and negative confirmation tokens
